newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia still studying corn import duty-minister.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia still studying corn import duty-minister.

text.p: Indonesian Agriculture Minister Syarifuddin Baharsyah said on Wednesday the government was still studying whether to impose an import duty on corn or find other ways of boosting domestic prices.

"We are still studying whether to impose a tariff or find other ways. We must be carefull on this issue. I will discuss it with the appropriate ministers," Baharsyah told Reuters before the monthly cabinet meeting on the economy.

He has said he wanted the government to impose an import tariff on corn because of poor domestic prices. Information Minister Harmoko said on Wednesday that President Suharto had ordered related ministers to study ways to protect domestic corn producers.

"Farmers are encouraged to plant corn. The president has ordered the appropriate ministers to find ways so farmers continue to be encouraged (to plant corn) and improve farm income," Harmoko told reporters after cabinet meeting.
"The related ministers should study how far the corn importers can buy domestic corn production," Harmoko said.
Baharsyah said Indonesia's corn production was expected to increase to about 10.5 million tonnes in 1997 from 9.1 million tonnes last year,
Indonesia, in a bid to reduce its dependence on imported corn, has embarked on an ambitious programme to boost local production through the cultivation of a high-yielding hybrid.
A agriculture ministry official said in January that a total of 885,000 hectares would be planted with the hybrid variety this year, and another 900,000 hectares in 1998.
Traders said Indonesia imported around 1.6 million tonnes of corn in 1996.
They said 1997 imports were expected to remain at last year's level because the success of the hybrid project had been overstated and that corn demand was growing rapidly.
